stocks.note: Numbers as of market close on Friday, May 22nd. U.S. markets were closed Monday for Memorial Day.
stocks.news:
All three indices closed Friday in the green. Huawei revealed a new chip design heading into smartphones this fall, right after Nvidia (NVDA -1.90%) CEO Jensen Huang said he is no longer planning to grow Nvidia's footprint in China. U.S. export rules pushed Nvidia's top chips out of the market, and Huawei is chipping away at the share that was left behind.

Disney's lightsaber dimmed. Disney (DIS -0.56%) opened "Mandalorian and Grogu" to $82M, the lowest Star Wars debut of the Disney era. It beat the $80M forecast but trailed 2018's "Solo." The franchise isn't broken; it's just not what it was when Baby Yoda was still a surprise.

economy.note: US 10-Year and Gold as of 4:00 PM ET Monday, May 25th. WTI Crude reflects today's intraday move via investing.com.
economy.commentary:
The 10-year is at 4.51%, 14 basis points below where it sat a week ago. WTI sits at $93.74, down $2.86 from yesterday but already up nearly three dollars from its $90.93 open after traders spent the morning panicking and the afternoon changing their minds. Carlyle's top economist said this week that global oil supply is "running on fumes" and that the U.S. could run short by July 2027; the IEA flagged the same window.

Gold continues its quiet bid. Spot gold jumped 1.1% to $4,539 Monday as Iran peace hopes pushed the dollar to one-week lows. Silver, platinum, and palladium all joined the move. Gold continues to behave as if it has been told a recession is on the way, and is waiting patiently for the rest of the market to agree.

crypto.note: Numbers as of 4:00 PM ET on Monday, May 25th.
crypto.commentary:
Crypto closed Monday tight: BTC flat, ETH and XRP slightly red. The SEC paused its plan to let crypto firms mint on-chain token versions of stocks like Apple (AAPL +1.26%) without the issuer's sign-off, after stock-exchange officials pushed back. For now, the on-chain stock market remains a slide deck.

The CLARITY Act, still moving through Congress, would ban platforms from paying users a yield just for holding a token or stablecoin, the model behind Celsius and BlockFi. Pure staking yields would survive; the platforms that paid you to do nothing would not.

real_estate.homebuilder: Rates Ease A Second Time To 6.61%; April Contract Signings Up A Third Straight Month; Tri-County Holds At 2,912 The Morning After Memorial Day
real_estate.commentary:
The 30-year fixed is at 6.61% today, down 4 bps from Friday's 6.65%. The 15-year sits at 6.14%, down 9 bps. The two-day move on the 30-year is now off 10 bps, the cleanest run of relief this month. The 10-year Treasury closed Monday at 4.51%, off 6 bps from Friday.

Local Tri-County board: 2,912 active, down 19 from Friday. 188 new listings hit this morning (vs 196 Friday), and closed sales over the rolling 7-day window jumped to 262, up 23. The closing pace is accelerating into late May, holiday or not.

📍 Alameda & Contra Costa Snapshot (05/26/26)

📍 Fremont: 16 new. Down 2 from Friday's 18.

📍 Union City: 8 new. Up 2 from 6.

📍 Newark: 5 new. Down 1 from 6.

📍 Hayward: 15 new. Up 2 from 13.

📍 Danville: 17 new. Down 1 from 18.

📍 Milpitas: 2 new. Down 1 from 3.

📍 Oakland: 50 new. Down 1 from 51, board leader continues.

📍 Livermore: 17 new. Down 2 from 19.

📍 Castro Valley: 8 new. Down 1 from 9.

📍 Pleasanton: 5 new. Down 1 from 6.

📍 San Ramon: 17 new. Flat.

📍 Dublin: 18 new. Down 3 from 21.

📍 Sunol: 1 new. Flat.

📍 San Lorenzo: 2 new. Flat.

📍 San Leandro: 7 new. Up 1 from 6.

9 of 15 cities pulled back, most by 1 to 3. San Leandro and Union City are the only meaningful adds. Exactly the board you would expect on the Tuesday after Memorial Day: sellers easing back in, not racing.

National context. April contract signings ran 3.2% ahead of last year despite climbing rates, the third straight month of gains. Hartford, Connecticut is now the hottest housing market in the country per Zillow, with inventory 63% below pre-pandemic levels. Hartford spent two decades as the punchline of New England real estate; turns out scarcity will fix a reputation faster than any chamber of commerce can.

For agents. Closed sales up 23 over the week, contract signings up nationally for a third straight month, and a -10 bp two-day rate move that is worth about $65 a month on a $1M loan. Pricing to today is the move for sellers; locking pre-approvals at today's rate is the move for buyers.
